transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because my sleep has gotten completely out of control. At first I’d sleep maybe two or three hours, then I’d be up making plans, feeling like I was ready to go. Now it’s more like I’m lying awake before dawn, my stomach all tight, and I don’t feel rested at all.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t see.
During these times when you sleep only a few hours, do you feel unusually happy or high?

Yes. For weeks I felt almost… brilliantly optimistic, like nothing could really get in my way and every problem was easy to solve. But it wasn’t just happy. If anyone questioned me, I’d snap at them, like they were trying to undermine me when I was the only one thinking clearly.
When you were sleeping only two or three hours, did you still feel fully rested?

At first, yes — that was the strange part. I’d sleep two or three hours and wake up feeling ready to go, like I didn’t need more. But now it’s changed. I’m awake before dawn, tense in my stomach, and I don’t feel rested at all.
During that time, were you much more active than usual?

Yes, definitely. I felt like there was an engine running inside me. I couldn’t just sit still. I’d be up before sunrise calling people, rewriting proposals, jumping from one thing to the next without really stopping.
During that high-energy period, were you hospitalized because of it?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I don’t think I have anything specific to say about being hospitalized for it.
During that high-energy period, did it cause serious problems in your life?

Yes. It’s caused real problems. My wife has had to take over the finances, and she’s been staying close to me because she’s worried about my safety. And I’ve stopped being reliable with things I used to keep up with — the museum, the arts council, even friends. I just haven’t been showing up the way I should.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
Yes. It’s been much longer than two weeks. Since those plans fell apart, I’ve been in this low, guilty place and mostly withdrawn… for about nine months now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar affective disorder with a current manic episode without psychotic symptoms. The patient describes a sustained period of elevated/expansive mood with irritability, markedly decreased need for sleep, increased energy and activity, and significant functional impairment. Psychotic symptoms were denied. A prolonged depressive period was also reported, supporting bipolar illness rather than an isolated manic episode.
